newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ money markets ignore TWI recovery, end weak.
newsitem.headline: NZ money markets ignore TWI recovery, end weak.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 9.34 PCT (PREV 9.35) US 5-YR 5.90 (PREV 5.90)
* NZ money markets ignore bounce in TWI, end weak
* Volumes average
* Bonds quiet with U.S. out of play, end flat
New Zealand money markets finished the session weaker on Thursday, never quite recovering from early weakness in the currency.
The kiwi dollar's Trade-Weighted Index bounced back up to 66.80 at the close from its 66.63 open, but the 90-day bank bills ended on their open of 8.80 percent.
The December futures contract closed five points lower at 91.53.
One dealer said the market's underlying tone had improved even if this hadn't been reflected in closing levels.
"It's feeling a little bit long and has consolidated a little bit today, then come back bid in the afternoon with the currency coming up.
"Generally there's still quite an underlying bullish note to things, obviously everyone is watching for the futures close out and also the monetary policy statement."
The market expects the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to ease conditions in the December 17 statement.
The cash rate settled back to 9.35 percent at the close from 9.50 earlier in the session, but dealers said cash conditions remained extremely tight.

"There has been inverse pricing in the cash for a week -- there's just one player sitting there on the cash, and everyone else is basically defending where it should probably be. It's quite easy to push the cash rate up at the moment, and it's ridiculously high -- cash should probably be settling more around nine percent," one said.

Meanwhile, short and bonds closed slightly weaker and the longer maturities ended flat. Dealers said there was a lack of direction with the U.S. Treasury market out of action for Thanksgiving Day and light trade in Asian markets, and the market was looking for new flows.
